projects.title: C7 Active Aero Design & Fabrication
projects.intro: Composite structures, aluminum hardware and vehicle packaging, followed by an actuator experiment that revealed a speed-versus-holding tradeoff.
projects.stage: Built hardware · Servo bench + road evaluation

Servo actuation experiment — stationary response test; road testing exposed inadequate holding torque.

story.label: What I built
items: Used 3D-printed prototypes to check wing geometry, brackets and vehicle packaging before fabricating carbon-composite structures and aluminum hardware.
Developed movable front aero and integrated actuation and feedback into the vehicle.

story.label: What I tested
story.text: I evaluated servo motors as an alternative to linear actuators. The servo setup delivered much faster motion and response in bench testing.

story.label: What road testing revealed
story.text: The tested servo setup lacked self-locking capability and sufficient holding torque to resist aerodynamic loading. A higher-torque servo setup or faster linear actuator remains a candidate for further evaluation.

projects.title: CAN / ESP32 Control: From Design to V2 Hardware
projects.intro: A modular V2 controller prototype, designed, hand-assembled, integrated and debugged by me.

feature.caption: V2 active-aero controller — assembled module-based PCB and bench wiring.

support.caption: Controller PCB 3D design — planning module integration.
V2 controller during hand assembly after JLC board fabrication.
Hands-on assembly of my V2 active-aero controller prototype.

story.label: My contribution
items: Designed the PCB, had it fabricated by JLC, then soldered, integrated and debugged the prototype myself.
Integrated ESP32 + MCP2515 CAN with throttle, brake, wheel-speed and steering-wheel inputs.
Implemented position feedback, deadband, watchdog behavior, STOP priority and automatic / manual modes.

story.label: Development approach
story.text: V2 uses a custom board to bring proven modules together as a step toward a more fully integrated PCB.

story.label: How I validated it
story.text: The V2 controller underwent bench and road testing. The earlier V1 active-aero system was used on track; V2 has not yet been track-tested.

story.label: What I prototyped
story.text: Bench-tested a four-node concept combining visible cameras and infrared thermal sensing, with an ESP32-P4 serving as the HMI.

story.label: How the direction evolved
story.text: I later narrowed the scope to infrared-only tire-temperature sensing with an iPhone or iPad HMI. The P4 and visible-camera media document the earlier architecture.

story.label: Development stage
story.text: Thermal sensing remains at the bench-testing stage. Broader instrumentation work includes suspension-travel sensing and strain / HX711 load-measurement concepts.

story.label: How I validate and iterate
items: Run the C7 at Gingerman and Grattan and review PDR / Pi Toolbox data after sessions.
Use suspension-travel behavior and observed limits to investigate aero balance, ride-height sensitivity and high-speed understeer.
Perform trackside troubleshooting, service work and setup checks as part of the development loop.

story.label: Version context
story.text: The track-tested active-aero configuration is V1. V2 controller testing covers bench and road use; the thermal-sensing project remains at the bench stage.
